summary.title: Breakout
summary.one_liner: This page introduces a multi-chapter series on building a 2D Breakout-style arcade game with modern OpenGL.
keywords: how to make a game with opengl
takeaways: Breakout's core mechanics: a horizontal paddle, a ball that changes direction based on hit position, and bricks destroyed on contact.
The series builds a complete 2D game rendered on the GPU using OpenGL.
Planned extras include particles, text rendering, power-ups, postprocessing effects, and customizable levels.
The series assumes you have finished the Getting Started chapters and draws on concepts from earlier chapters.
summary.summary: This is the introduction to a LearnOpenGL series that turns the classic Atari Breakout arcade game into a practical OpenGL project. It describes the original game mechanics, such as paddle control, ball bounce physics, brick destruction, and win/lose conditions. It then lists the extra features the series will add, including particles, text rendering, power-ups, postprocessing, and multiple levels. The page is a preview with no code, and it points readers to the Getting Started chapters as prerequisites.
